findings.issue_text: Blacklisted emails are lowercased but submitted emails are not normalized before comparison, allowing uppercase or mixed-case inputs to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS
The server does not enforce unique input emails or deduplicate guests, so direct API calls with duplicate addresses create duplicate attendee records and invitations
“Admin or owner” authorization uses isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner, incorrectly denying team admins who are not the booking organizer
Attendees are saved before the external calendar update, so a calendar update failure leaves guests in the booking without calendar additions or notifications
Email classification uses the original guests input instead of uniqueGuests, causing an already-attending address submitted with a new guest to receive a new-booking confirmation email

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attendees are saved before the external calendar update, so a calendar update failure leaves guests in the booking without calendar additions or notifications

adjudication.rationale: Looking at addGuests.handler.ts, the code flow is: 1) prisma.booking.update() adds guests to the database (lines 85-99), 2) eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees() updates external calendar (line 163), 3) sendAddGuestsEmails() sends notifications (line 167). If step 2 fails, the guests are already persisted in the database but the calendar wasn't updated. There's no transaction or rollback mechanism. The try-catch only wraps the email sending, not the calendar update. This is a real consistency bug where partial state can occur.
